title: Slav Defense: the ideas
line: A pawn on c6 holds the center, and the bishop stays free to come out.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares too. It holds the center.

also.g8f6: That is the start of the Indian defenses, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.after: White offers a side pawn to pull your center pawn away. This is the Queen's Gambit.

steps.text: Guard your center pawn with the pawn on c7. Your bishop on c8 stays free to come out.

also.e7e6: That guards it too, the Queen's Gambit Declined. This lesson guards with the other pawn.
also.d5c4: That is the Queen's Gambit Accepted, also sound. This lesson keeps the center pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It guards the center pawn too.

also.e7e6: That heads for the Semi-Slav, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out first.
also.d5c4: Taking the pawn is sound too. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.after: White moves its king pawn, and its own bishop on c1 is now behind its pawns.

steps.text: Bring your bishop out now, before you move the king pawn.
steps.after: That is the Slav's point: the bishop is outside the pawns.

steps.text: Now move the pawn in front of your king one square. It frees your other bishop and guards the center.
steps.after: White's knight goes after your bishop.

steps.text: Step the bishop back. If the knight takes it, your pawn on h7 takes back, and your rook looks down the h-file.

also.f5e4: That keeps the bishop safe too. This lesson steps back to the other square.

steps.after: Black's pawns hold the center, and the bishop from c8 is outside the pawn chain.

summary: A side pawn guards the center pawn, so the bishop comes out before the king pawn moves.
